stimulus.text:
Population of leading American cities (U.S. Bureau of the Census)

| City | 1870 | 1890 |
| New York | 942,292 | 1,515,301 |
| Chicago | 298,977 | 1,099,850 |
| Philadelphia | 674,022 | 1,046,964 |
| St. Louis | 310,864 | 451,770 |
| Boston | 250,526 | 448,477 |

Populations are from the decennial census of each year.
stimulus.source_note: U.S. Bureau of the Census, Population of the 100 Largest Urban Places, 1870 and 1890. Public data.

source: original; stimulus verified against its source (see source_note)

books.section: Topic 6.8 Immigration and Migration in the Gilded Age
The Rise of the Modern American City

primary_sources: U.S. Bureau of the Census, Population of the 100 Largest Urban Places, 1870 and 1890

stem: The table best supports which claim about American cities in the Gilded Age?

options.text: Cities in the South grew faster than cities in the North
options.misconception: Compares regions the table never shows.

options.text: New York lost population while Chicago gained it
options.misconception: Turns New York’s gain of 573,000 into a loss.

options.text: Most Americans still lived on farms in 1890
options.misconception: Reads farm life out of a table that counts only cities.

options.text: Industrial cities in the Northeast and Midwest grew rapidly

rationales.A: No Southern city is in the table. Nothing here compares the South with the North.
rationales.B: New York grew from 942,292 to 1,515,301. It gained, not lost.
rationales.C: The table counts city people only. It says nothing about how many Americans lived on farms.
rationales.D: Every city in the table grew, and Chicago nearly quadrupled, so the industrial cities of the Northeast and Midwest grew fast.
rationales.general:
Ask what all five rows have in common.
1. Every city in the table grew between 1870 and 1890.
2. Chicago nearly quadrupled, and New York added over half a million people.
3. All five are Northeastern or Midwestern cities.
4. Shared rapid growth in one region is the claim the table supports.
Remember: a claim a table supports must fit every row, not one row.
